_note: What each town sells, for ever. A shelf is content: it does not roll, it does not reroll, and a save records only which entries have been bought. Order is part of the contract — a purchase is stored as a town and an index — so append to a list, never insert into the middle of one.
_shape: Each town is a place rather than a slot machine in a costume. The End of All Gears has the cheap basics and nothing else; Kettleworks is metalwork, and is where a real helmet and a second blade come from; High Wick is the arcane shelf and the only place a book, an ink and a spell can be bought together - and it is on no map, which is why the barrel had to be the counter that carries the casting family. Neither placed town sells arcana, on purpose: a town is its character, and the barrel is under every counter and is nobody's character.
_barrel: The barrel under the counter, and it is the same barrel in every town. It never runs out, so nothing here is an index a save records and buying from it writes nothing down - which is why this block has no seam. It is the shop's floor and not more of its ceiling: every entry is cheap, small and the lowest-rated of its kind at four cells and `shop::BARREL_CEILING` - sixty Fnorp - or under. Its shape is `shop::barrel_wants`, which is derived from the recipe table rather than listed here: one of each kind every recipe needs, as many of each as it asks for, and two of the things a recipe will take. That is fourteen cores and two extras, and it covers all THREE ways of building a weapon - a blade, a book and a crystal ball - where the old hand-written list covered the blade and left a hundred and six casting components on no counter in the game. A rerolled barrel has the same shape, because it is rolled from the same wants.
_commissions: What each town will make to order. Paid up front, arrives after that many fights, and collected in person at the counter that took it - one open order per town. Priced at COMMISSION_PCT of the catalogue, which is twice the shelf: ordering certainty costs more than finding luck. Nothing here is on a shelf or in the barrel, so an order is a third source and not a slower way to shop.

towns._note: The pit's own town, and everything on it is under a hundred and thirty Fnorp. A starting character has a hundred and forty and owns a handle and a blade, so this shelf is one finished helmet and one pair of gloves, or most of both.
Metalwork. Plate, gauntlets and edges — the things the slag flats are made of.
The arcane shelf, and the only one that sells a book, an ink and a spell in the same room — which is the whole of what makes a caster weapon buildable at all.

**Empty on purpose, and `avail.rs`'s `UNWRITTEN` is where that is written down.** PLAN-M14.md §1.5: the third town ships with a name, a start tile and a region, and nothing to buy — a shelf invented to keep a lint quiet would be content nobody asked for standing where the content that was asked for has to go.
